Calcium carbonate nanoparticles dissociated to release Ca 2+ , which cross-linked with alginate, thereby enhancing the mechanical properties of the gel. The bioinspired reinforced hydrogel exhibited smooth extrudability and stable embolization. Additionally, the introduction of iron oxide endowed the hydrogel with magnetic field responsiveness, enabling tumor hyperthermia. Given the unique advantages, the bioinspired reinforced hydrogel holds a promise as novel embolic agents for hepatocellular carcinoma treatment.

title: Astrocytic Sirt2-Mediated Delactylation Limits Blood–Spinal Cord Barrier Reconstruction after Spinal Cord Injury
abstract: Restoration of the blood–spinal cord barrier (BSCB) is required for substantial neurological improvement after spinal cord injury (SCI). Astrocytes are integral to this barrier and, after injury, undergo glycolytic adaptation accompanied by lactate accumulation. Whether a lactate-linked modification program in astrocytes participates in BSCB repair has remained unresolved. Here, we identify astrocytic delactylation as a brake on BSCB repair. Sirtuin2 (Sirt2), a delactylase, was strongly induced in astrocytes at the lesion border, and its expression paralleled the pathological expansion of microvessels. Selective deletion of Sirt2 in astrocytes increased lactylation, produced a lactate-rich metabolic state, attenuated inflammatory astrocyte programs, enhanced repair-associated features, and reinforced BSCB repair. These changes further reduced inflammatory infiltration and promoted neuronal retention, increased 5-hydroxytryptamine-positive fiber density, and improved locomotor recovery. Pharmacological Sirt2 inhibition produced similar vascular and locomotor benefits. Mechanistically, Sirt2 loss elevated H4K8la occupancy at the hepatocyte growth factor ( Hgf ) locus and promoted Hgf transcription, thereby facilitating BSCB repair. Astrocyte-specific Sirt2 ablation also weakened CD8 + T-cell-related inflammatory activity after SCI. Collectively, our findings position astrocytic Sirt2 -dependent delactylation as a negative epigenetic–metabolic regulator of BSCB reconstruction and support astrocytic delactylation as a therapeutic target for SCI.

title: General Collaborative Intelligence: Architecting Cognition for Resilient Multi-Agent Ecosystems
abstract: Multi-agent unmanned systems are moving from isolated, ego-centric sensing toward collaborative intelligence, in which distributed agents exchange compact features to overcome a local observation trap that no single agent can escape: occlusions, finite sensor range, and environmental degradation. The field has matured across architectural, communication, embodied, resilience, and trust dimensions, yet existing surveys examine these dimensions in isolation and rarely expose their dependencies. This review offers a unified synthesis through two complementary lenses. The first is a five-dimensional taxonomy spanning collaboration stage, communication paradigm, fusion architecture, learning strategy, and application domain. The second is three cognitive synergy conditions, Semantic Disambiguation, Pragmatic Information Exchange, and Proactive Informational Foraging, that turn cognitive synergy into operational criteria. Across these lenses we survey collaboration architectures and topologies, neural-communication co-design that treats the channel as a differentiable pipeline component, embodied action-perception loops via multi-agent reinforcement learning, and resilience mechanisms for synchronization, uncertainty quantification, and label-efficient learning. We then map these advances onto four operational domains, V2X, unmanned aerial, industrial logistics, and smart cities, and onto the safety-privacy-utility triad. To counter benchmark saturation and evaluation fragmentation, we propose GCI-Bench, a five-pillar scoring protocol with a maturity model that makes the trade-offs of collaborative methods comparable across studies. A critical reflection on reproducibility, the sim-to-real gulf, and conditions under which collaboration degrades performance identifies open challenges and charts directions toward general collaborative intelligence under real-world uncertainty.

title: Scoparone-Induced Phase Separation of ZDHHC12 Drives Ferroptosis via ATG12 S-palmitoylation and Ferritinophagy in Liver Fibrosis
abstract: Activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are central effectors of liver fibrogenesis, and their selective elimination is critical for fibrosis regression. Although ferroptotic clearance of HSCs has emerged as a promising antifibrotic strategy, the upstream mechanisms coupling metabolic remodeling to ferroptosis susceptibility remain unclear. This study investigated whether scoparone (SCO) suppresses liver fibrosis through zinc finger DHHC-type palmitoyltransferase 12 (ZDHHC12) condensate formation, leading to enhanced autophagy-related protein 12 (ATG12) S-palmitoylation, induction of autophagy, and increased ferroptosis susceptibility in HSCs. We found that SCO restrained cell proliferation, migration, and fibrogenic activation while inducing iron overload, lipid peroxidation, glutathione depletion, and ferroptosis-like mitochondrial remodeling. Metabolomic and S-palmitoylation analyses linked these effects to increased palmitic acid levels and enhanced global protein S-palmitoylation. ZDHHC12 emerged as a SCO-responsive palmitoyltransferase associated with autophagy activation, ferritin turnover, ferroptosis induction, and repression of fibrogenic markers. Mechanistically, SCO promoted the formation of liquid-like ZDHHC12 condensates, which enhanced its interaction with ATG12 and facilitated ATG12 S-palmitoylation at the conserved Cys134 residue. This modification was associated with increased ATG12 stability through reduced ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation, thereby promoting autophagy activation and increasing ferroptosis susceptibility in HSCs. Mutation of ATG12 at Cys134 attenuated these effects and diminished HSC ferroptosis. In cholestatic and toxic models of liver fibrosis, SCO alleviated liver injury and collagen deposition, whereas HSC-targeted silencing of ZDHHC12 or ATG12 attenuated these protective effects, supporting biological consistency in vivo. Integrated bioinformatic and clinical cohort analyses suggested that ZDHHC12 expression positively correlated with ATG12 expression and was associated with fibrosis progression in patients with liver fibrosis. Collectively, these findings support a ZDHHC12-dependent ATG12 S-palmitoylation pathway linking lipid metabolic remodeling to autophagy-mediated ferroptosis in HSCs and suggest phase-regulated S-palmitoylation as a potential antifibrotic target.

title: Microalgal Synthetic Biotechnology: From Genetic Models to Deployable Photosynthetic Chassis
abstract: Microalgae have long been considered promising platforms for producing biochemicals and supporting environmental applications. Realizing this potential will require turning microalgal species into predictable and reusable engineering platforms. However, it remains challenging to engineer such evolutionarily diverse, compartmentalized photosynthetic eukaryotes in a predictable way, because their behavior depends strongly on organelle organization, gene-expression context, and cultivation conditions. Here, we focus on 3 well-developed but functionally distinct chassis. Chlamydomonas reinhardtii provides the strongest genetic and cell-biological foundation among green microalgae; Phaeodactylum tricornutum serves as the main diatom system for genome engineering and systems-level pathway analysis; and Nannochloropsis spp., especially N. oceanica and N. gaditana , are more production-oriented and are particularly important for lipid engineering. We assess these chassis from the perspective of practical engineerability, including transformation and genome access, expression design, precise editing and regulatory control, and iterative design–build–test–learn workflows. We then discuss 4 representative trait areas: photosynthetic productivity and stress tolerance, storage lipids and omega-3 fatty acids, terpenoids and carotenoids, and pollutant removal. Despite substantial progress, the field is still limited by unstable transgene expression, weak portability of genetic parts, incomplete understanding of intracellular pathway organization, and poor agreement between laboratory phenotypes and process performance. Progress will require genetic design to be evaluated together with chassis physiology, cultivation performance, product recovery, and deployment-specific biosafety.

title: Laser Vibrometry and Dispersion Analysis-Enabled Mechanical Property Characterization for Additively Manufactured Thermoset Composites
abstract: Large-format additive manufacturing of thermoset composites enables rapid fabrication of large structures, but nondestructive characterization of their print-path-dependent mechanical behavior remains difficult. Existing qualification routes rely mainly on destructive coupon testing or defect-oriented nondestructive evaluation and therefore provide limited capability for targeted mapping of direction-dependent mechanical variability. This study presents a piezoelectric transducer–laser Doppler vibrometry framework for direction-conditioned dispersion inversion of full-field guided wave measurements in additively manufactured thermoset composites. The method decomposes the frequency–wavenumber spectrum by propagation angle and independently fits the extracted dispersion data in each propagation direction to obtain scan-region-specific effective shear-wave velocity, an effective Poisson’s-ratio parameter, and effective-modulus responses as functions of propagation direction. Benchmark testing on an isotropic aluminum plate validates that the workflow recovers isotropic guided wave behavior without introducing artificial angular bias. Applied to a chopped-carbon-fiber thermoset composite, the framework reveals print-path-dependent anisotropic wave propagation through elliptical wavefields and frequency–wavenumber spectra. The resulting effective stiffness estimates reproduce the direction-dependent stiffness variation and approximate magnitude observed in conventional tensile measurements, supporting the mechanical relevance of the guided wave-derived response. By converting full-field guided wave measurements into scan-region-specific, direction-resolved effective-stiffness estimates, this work provides a practical nondestructive route to support quality control, process validation, and structural evaluation of aerospace composite tooling manufactured by large-format thermoset additive manufacturing.

title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps-Mediated Intraplaque Angiogenesis and Microvascular Permeability Promote Rapid Plaque Progression following Myocardial Infarction
abstract: Despite adherence to guideline-recommended therapies, survivors of myocardial infarction (MI) remain at high risk for recurrent ischemic events. This study aimed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms responsible for this residual risk. Using Mendelian randomization analysis and retrospective cohort study, we established a causal relationship between MI and plaque progression, potentially mediated by neutrophils. In a murine atherosclerotic model, MI precipitated a marked expansion in plaque volume accompanied by reduced stability; these pathological changes are consistent with the hallmark features of rapid plaque progression, which may trigger recurrent ischemic events. Pharmacological inhibition and adoptive transfer experiments using Padi4 flox/flox Lyz2 Cre mice confirmed the pivotal role of neutrophils in MI-driven rapid plaque progression via neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation. Further investigations revealed that NETs promote intraplaque hemorrhage by facilitating intraplaque angiogenesis and enhancing microvascular permeability, thereby exacerbating post-MI atherosclerotic inflammation. Mechanistically, bioinformatics analyses and in vitro experiments identified the transcription factor ETS proto-oncogene 1 as a critical regulator of NETs-mediated angiogenesis and endothelial permeability through the activation of the vascular endothelial growth factor A/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 signaling pathway. In vivo pharmacological inhibition of ETS proto-oncogene 1 with TK216 markedly attenuated the rapid plaque progression after MI. In summary, this study provides the first comprehensive evidence that neutrophils and NETs drive rapid plaque progression following MI by modulating intraplaque angiogenesis and hemorrhage. These findings offer novel insights into the mechanisms underlying post-MI ischemic event recurrence and highlight promising therapeutic targets for clinical prevention.

title: Thermoelectric Cement Composite Materials for Energy Harvesting and Self-Powered Sensing
abstract: The share of building energy consumption in global total energy consumption continues to rise. Transforming building envelopes into media for low-grade heat harvesting and self-powered sensing has therefore become one of the key technological pathways toward achieving the “dual carbon” goals. In recent years, ionic thermoelectric (i-TE) materials have attracted widespread attention due to their operational capability under low temperature gradients, readily available raw materials, and high thermoelectric potential. Endowing commodity building materials with i-TE functionality offers an effective strategy for low-grade waste heat harvesting in buildings and their low-carbon transition. Cement-based materials, owing to their natural porous structure, abundant pore solution ions, and multiphase solid–liquid interfacial environment, exhibit unique potential as i-TE media. This paper systematically reviews the research progress on the i-TE performance of i-TE cement-based composites (i-TECs). The core mechanisms of the thermodiffusion effect and thermogalvanic effect are explained, and a framework for evaluating key performance parameters is established. The paper examines how the intrinsic properties of the cement matrix govern i-TE behavior and summarizes the strategies currently employed to optimize performance. The applications of i-TECs in building energy harvesting, self-powered temperature sensing, and structural supercapacitor energy storage are surveyed, highlighting the multifunctional potential of these materials. Finally, this review outlines the key challenges in guiding the rational development of durable and efficient i-TECs, and provides an outlook on the development prospects and engineering application potential.

title: The Ratio of Silicon to Chitin in Diatom Cell Walls Influences Their Resilience to Environmental Stress
abstract: The diatom cell wall is a critically protective barrier against biotic and abiotic stress, yet the mechanisms by which its individual components confer resilience remain elusive. Using the model diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana , we show that resting cells chemically remodel their cell wall by increasing the ratio of silicon to chitin. Our integrative approach, based on a combination of transcriptomics, cell biology, and reverse genetics, reveals that the girdle-band-associated protein cingulin W2 (CinW2) directly regulates the biochemical cell wall composition, driving a “high silicon–low chitin” phenotype under abiotic and biotic stress. The regulation of the gene encoding CinW2 is controlled by an AP2-family transcription factor (AP2-1) that also modulates a chitinase, thereby orchestrating the compositional shift. This shift supporting a silicon-rich frustule provides enhanced structural reinforcement, substantially improving the resilience of T. pseudonana under biotic and abiotic stress. Tara Oceans metatranscriptome data suggest that genes involved in adjusting the ratio of silicon to chitin are widespread across diatom lineages and their expression appears to be responsive to changing environmental conditions in surface oceans. Although the CinW2-mediated regulatory mechanism has been identified only in the genus Thalassiosira , we have identified coregulated homologs in diverse diatom lineages. Collectively, our data therefore suggest that the molecular mechanism by which T. pseudonana modulates key cell wall components might represent a common strategy to cope with challenging environmental conditions.

title: Cancer Hacks Neurodegeneration: Cystatin-C as a Bridge for Microglial Amyloid Clearance via TREM2
abstract: Historically, epidemiological studies have consistently highlighted an inverse correlation between cancer and Alzheimer’s disease, yet the molecular link between these 2 distinct pathologies remained elusive. In a recent breakthrough published in Cell , Li et al. provide a compelling answer by revealing that peripheral tumors secrete cystatin-C, which binds to preexisting amyloid oligomers and activates triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) in microglia, leading to the clearance of preexisting amyloid plaques in Alzheimer’s disease mice.

title: Artificial Intelligence as Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance
A Bioinspired Cellulosic Elastomer with Ultrahigh Robustness Enabled by Structure-Induced Reconstruction for Impact Protection
abstract: Elastomers that combine high strength, exceptional toughness, self-healing capability, and scalable processability remain difficult to achieve. Here, we report a leech-inspired cellulosic elastomer constructed from cellulose, diatomite, and polyacrylamide through ethanol-induced structural reconstruction. The resulting bioinspired elastomer exhibits enhanced mechanical performance and efficient energy dissipation, with nearly complete compressive recoverability, a compressive strength above 90 MPa, and a load-bearing capacity exceeding 160,000 times its own weight. The elastomer further demonstrates high resistance to static puncture and dynamic impact, with a puncture resistance energy of 304.22 mJ and an impact toughness of 28.62 MJ m −3 , while maintaining self-healing capability without thermal treatment and tolerance to ultralow temperatures down to −196 °C. In addition, the elastomer is compatible with roll-to-roll manufacturing and can be produced at the meter scale at a low cost. This work offers a scalable strategy for fabricating robust elastomers with potential applications in advanced impact protection and emerging soft technologies.

title: Positioning Creation of Cell Communication Channels via Chinese Microneedle
abstract: The core dilemma of senescence mitigation lies in the disrupted and even detrimental communication between senescent cells and local immune cells. Existing delivery methods cannot precisely establish protective intercellular communication channels across cell types within the enclosed lesion cavity. In this study, we utilize Chinese microneedle technology for precise, minimally invasive localization of aged lesions, and to release spatially targeted and temporally sustained dual-field to create intercellular communication channels between macrophages and senescent cells. The unique physical properties of this Chinese microneedle system confine the current path to specific spatiotemporal windows, releasing an electro-field while simultaneously activating dynamic van der Waals forces that release functionalized hydrogel microparticles, thereby superimposing a vita-field. Within the dual-field active zone, the electro-field not only attenuates cellular senescence but also forms a communication channel from senescent cells to macrophages, driving macrophages into a hyperactivated state. Meanwhile, the vita-field stabilizes the macrophage membrane, enabling long-term, stable communication between hyperactivated macrophages and senescent cells. Ultimately, the intercellular communication channels established by this Chinese microneedle system alleviate cellular senescence and apoptosis, supporting the repair of aged lesions.

title: Programmable Spatiotemporal Magnetic Fields for Selective Multimodal Actuation and Deterministic Decoupling of Heterogeneous Magnetic Robots
abstract: Magnetic milli/microrobots hold strong potential for biomedical applications, but their deployment as multi-robot systems is limited by short-range magnetic coupling, which prevents independent control in confined environments. Here, we present an expanded field-free region (FFR)-based control framework for spatially selective actuation of multiple magnetic torque-driven robots in confined environments. A generalized selective-control criterion incorporating the minimum rotating magnetic field required for robot actuation enables the framework to accommodate robots with different magnetic responses and operating conditions. Through programmable displacement and oscillation of the FFR, the framework extends conventional selective locomotion to include velocity regulation under a constant rotating magnetic field and oscillation-induced stick–slip locomotion. For strongly interacting permanent-magnet robots, a dedicated decoupling field reorients their magnetic moments to transition the inter-robot interaction from attraction to repulsion, enabling subsequent deterministic separation, whereas weakly interacting low-remanence robots can be separated using conventional FFR-based selective locomotion without dedicated decoupling. The framework is validated across different fluid viscosities and robots with distinct magnetic properties and is further integrated with robot redistribution and FFR-selective magnetic heating to achieve spatially regulated thermal responses. Finally, proof-of-concept demonstrations show clot-removal and targeted-delivery emulation and selective robot navigation in a 3-dimensional cerebrovascular phantom. These results establish an expanded FFR-based framework for sequential selective control of magnetic robots in confined environments and support its potential use in imaging-compatible robotic platforms for biomedical interventions.

title: Effect of Microcurrent Stimulation on Cartilage Regeneration in Engineered Chondrocyte Spheroids
abstract: Microcurrent stimulation has emerged as a promising biophysical cue for cartilage regeneration, but its dose-dependent effects in 3-dimensional engineered cartilage constructs remain unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of continuous direct microcurrent stimulation on auricular chondrocytes and engineered cartilage spheroids using 0-, 10-, 25-, 50-, 100-, and 200-μA stimulation for 30 min daily. In 2-dimensional culture, microcurrent stimulation did not markedly increase the DNA content or Cell Counting Kit-8 value, indicating that it did not markedly promote cell expansion or overall metabolic activity. 5-Ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine and Ki67 assays showed that low to moderate (<50 μA) stimulation had limited effects on proliferation, whereas 100 to 200 μA attenuated proliferative activity. Nevertheless, microcurrent stimulation enhanced chondrogenic marker expression in a biphasic manner, with type II collagen, SRY-box transcription factor 9, aggrecan, and cartilage oligomeric matrix protein increasing from 0 to 50 μA and declining from 50 to 200 μA. In 3-dimensional spheroids, 50 μA produced the most favorable morphology, cartilage-specific extracellular matrix deposition, mechanical properties, and hyaline cartilage-like phenotype. Excessive stimulation increased catabolic, inflammatory, and apoptosis-associated molecular responses without causing obvious cytotoxicity, apoptosis, reactive oxygen species production, temperature change, or pH alteration. Mechanistically, 50 μA induced coordinated Ca 2+ signaling and promoted nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT) nuclear translocation, whereas 200 μA generated dysregulated Ca 2+ responses and inefficient NFAT activation. Verapamil, 1,2-bis(2-aminophenoxy)ethane- N , N , N ′, N ′-tetraacetic acid acetoxymethyl ester, and cyclosporin A attenuated 50-μA-induced NFAT activation, supporting the involvement of the Ca 2+ /calcineurin/NFAT pathway. Furthermore, 50-μA-preconditioned spheroids showed superior cartilage-forming capacity after subcutaneous implantation. These findings identify 50 μA as a favorable bioelectrical stimulation condition within the tested intensity range and provide a practical strategy for enhancing cartilage spheroid maturation in cartilage tissue engineering.

title: Obesity-Induced PLPE–PTK6–FASN Feedback Loop Drives Enzalutamide Resistance by Exacerbating Lipid Metabolic Dysregulation in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
abstract: Obesity represents an independent risk factor for various malignancies, including prostate cancer. However, how specific lipid metabolites influence enzalutamide sensitivity in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) remains elusive. Here, we find that obesity is associated with poorer clinical outcomes during enzalutamide treatment. Lipidomic profiling reveals that 1-palmitoyl-2-linoleoyl phosphatidylethanolamine (PLPE) is markedly enriched in tumors from these individuals. Mechanistically, elevated PLPE directly binds to the SH2 domain of protein tyrosine kinase 6 (PTK6), driving its membrane translocation and functional activation. Furthermore, PLPE facilitates PTK6-fatty acid synthase (FASN) interaction, enabling PTK6 to mediate FASN phosphorylation at T976 via dual mechanisms: steric occupancy and kinase cascade amplification. This hyperactivation of FASN exacerbates lipid metabolic dysregulation, ultimately conferring enzalutamide resistance. Importantly, FASN-derived palmitic acid serves as a substrate for further PLPE synthesis, thereby reinforcing PTK6 membrane retention in a positive feedback loop. Collectively, this study identifies a PLPE–PTK6–FASN feedback loop that drives lipid metabolic reprogramming and enzalutamide resistance in CRPC with obesity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of cotargeting lipid metabolism and kinase signaling.

title: Railway-Integrated Planning of Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing Aircraft (eVTOL) Vertiports
abstract: Electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft provide a new and more sustainable form of mobility for passengers. In regional transport, eVTOL services can complement existing railway systems by providing direct air connections for selected trips. However, the practical value of eVTOL services is subject to strict infrastructure requirements beyond aircraft performance. Consequently, strategic vertiport deployment and charging capacity must be embedded into existing transport networks rather than planned as standalone systems. To achieve this objective, this paper presents a strategic railway-integrated planning framework for eVTOL vertiports and charging capacity. The framework treats railway stations as multimodal access nodes and leverages air links to selectively complement rail travel. It simultaneously optimizes siting, pad capacity, charging capacity, flight frequency, and fleet scale under infrastructure and operating constraints. To balance assignment fidelity and tractability in the integrated railway and air network, the framework applies a multicommodity flow (MCF) formulation for detailed network assignment and proposes a structured one-hop (SOH) formulation as a compact approximation. SOH restricts each substituted trip to a simple railway–air–rail (RAR) travel pattern with one direct air segment, thereby avoiding repeated intermodal transfers. Finally, the proposed framework is applied to scenario-based planning on a real-world railway network in Guangdong, China. The results show that all 11 sites selected by MCF are also selected by SOH, while SOH selects one additional site. The daily planning benefits obtained by MCF and SOH are 41,428 and 41,257 CNY/day, respectively, differing by only 0.4%, whereas SOH uses 93.5% fewer variables and reduces the solution time by 95.0%. Sensitivity analysis shows that no vertiport is selected when the transferable demand ratio is 1%. As the transferable demand ratio increases, both the planning benefit and the selected vertiport network increase until the site limit is reached.

title: Neural Organoids and Organoid Extracellular Vesicles for Spinal Cord Injury Repair
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes long-term disability in part because secondary injury progressively reshapes the lesion microenvironment and restricts axonal regeneration, circuit re-establishment, and white matter repair. Neural organoids are emerging from human pluripotent stem cell-derived disease models into implantable regenerative constructs that may provide structured cellular niches, support host–graft integration, and contribute to remyelination. However, their translation remains constrained by batch variability, limited vascularization, immune-related risk, and long-term safety concerns. In parallel, organoid-derived extracellular vesicles (OEVs) represent a cell-free modality linked to the organoid platform and are more amenable to controlled dosing and repeated administration. However, direct evidence supporting the therapeutic use of neural OEVs in SCI remains limited. OEVs should not be viewed as inherently superior alternatives to conventional extracellular vesicles (EVs); rather, their potential distinctiveness depends on experimentally verifiable links to source-organoid identity, developmental stage, multicellular context, and cargo–function logic. In SCI repair, current evidence should be stratified into direct evidence from neural OEV studies, supportive evidence from SCI-relevant conventional EV systems and related organoid/OEV studies, and testable translational hypotheses. This Review defines neural organoids and neural OEVs as source-linked but mechanistically non-equivalent repair modules, and proposes a mechanism-linked, stage-aware, and quality-oriented framework to guide OEV characterization, benchmarking, and translational evaluation for SCI repair.

title: Inverse Vaccine Nanomimics: In situ Antigen-Specific Immune Tolerance Induction for Durable Cardiac Repair Post-Myocardial Infarction
abstract: Alleviating the inflammatory response by inducing immune tolerance to cardiomyocyte lysate antigens has been shown to be a promising therapeutic approach for treating myocardial infarction (MI). However, immune tolerance induced by allogeneic antigens is constrained by insufficient antigen specificity, safety risks, and transient therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we present an injectable hydrogel capable of environment-responsive, long-acting delivery of inverse vaccine nanomimics (IVNMs) to overcome these challenges. These IVNMs efficiently capture antigens released by dying cardiomyocytes through the orthogonal reaction between surface maleimide groups and antigen thiols and promote mannose-facilitated uptake by CD206-expressing immune cells, including dendritic cells (DCs). The antigens captured by IVNMs, together with the sustained release of rapamycin from IVNMs, promote the differentiation of DCs into tolerogenic DCs, leading to a persistent increase in regulatory T cells and the establishment of immune tolerance memory. In post-MI rat models, myocardial inflammation was markedly and persistently alleviated, accompanied by enhanced neovascularization and reduced fibrosis, contributing to a sustained cardioprotective effect.

title: Overcoming the Curse of Dimensionality: Structural Connectivity Reconstruction via Pairwise Information Flow in Nonlinear Networks
Advances in Optical Nanoprobes for Bacterial Infection Diagnosis
abstract: Bacterial infections represent a major threat to global public health, and the rising prevalence of antibiotic resistance underscores the urgent need for early and accurate diagnosis. Optical imaging technologies, characterized by high sensitivity, spatiotemporal resolution, real-time monitoring capability, and noninvasiveness, have emerged as promising complementary and alternative approaches for bacterial infection diagnosis. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in optical nanoprobes for diagnosing bacterial infections. We first outline the structural and metabolic distinctions between bacteria and mammalian cells, along with the dynamic features of the infection microenvironment, which collectively provide a biological foundation for selective targeting and infection-specific imaging. We then detail the working principles, design strategies, and characteristics of various optical nanoprobes, including fluorescence, chemiluminescence, bioluminescence, photoacoustic, and Raman imaging probes, highlighting their applications in bacterial detection. Finally, we focus on in vitro diagnostic scenarios, categorizing and evaluating the performance, advantages, and challenges of optical nanoprobe-based technologies across clinical specimens such as blood, urine, and sputum. By offering a systematic perspective, this review aims to provide actionable insights for clinical translation and to promote the development of next-generation rapid diagnostic platforms for bacterial infections.

title: From Physiological Spaces to Cognitive Health: A New Perspective on Combined Acupuncture and Chinese Herbal Medicine for Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an escalating global health challenge. Although the target-centric paradigm focusing on targets such as β-amyloid (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, and neuroinflammation has advanced our understanding of AD, translated therapies remain limited in reversing disease progression. Viewing the brain through the lens of physiological spaces offers an alternative framework for re-evaluating AD pathogenesis. Under this theoretical model, the body comprises both physical structures (“entities”) and fluid-filled interstitial networks (“spaces”), with the latter facilitating metabolic transport, waste clearance, and intercellular signaling. Cerebral perivascular spaces, the extracellular space, and the glymphatic pathway represent specialized cranial interstitial networks. Fluid dynamic impairment within these spatial domains may serve as an upstream trigger for downstream Aβ aggregation, tau pathology, and neuroinflammatory cascades. Combining acupuncture with Chinese herbal medicine may restore fluid homeostasis and spatial patency across these networks. In a preliminary exploration study of 11 patients with mild-to-moderate AD, combined intervention showed encouraging trends toward improving cognitive performance and modulating relevant fluid biomarkers. This spatial perspective provides a complementary target for future AD disease-modifying strategies.

title: Terahertz Photons Ameliorate Traumatic Brain Injury and Reduce Neuroinflammation via the Cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate Signaling Pathway
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) has the highest incidence among common neurological disorders and remains the leading cause of mortality and disability among all kinds of injuries, yet specific therapies for TBI are still unavailable. In the present study, we found that short-term administration of terahertz (THz) photons during the acute phase of TBI ameliorated brain damage and cognitive deficits. THz photons induced a reduced population of microglia and an increased number of anti-inflammatory phenotypes of microglia. In vivo and in vitro validation further revealed that THz photons inhibit inflammasome activation. Blocking adenylyl cyclase type 9 (AC9) in microglia attenuated the beneficial effects of THz irradiation, indicating that THz-irradiation-mediated inhibition of inflammasome activation involves the AC9/cyclic adenosine monophosphate/NLR and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 signaling pathway. Compared with drug therapy, THz photon technology offers noninvasiveness, accurate tissue targeting, and on-demand application and removal. In conclusion, this study established a THz-photon-based therapeutic paradigm, highlighting its potential as a therapy for TBI and potentially other forms of acute brain injury.

title: Vitamin K1-Loaded Poly(Lactic-Co-Glycolic Acid)-Polyethylenimine Nanoparticles Promote Diabetic Wound Healing through FSP1-Dependent Suppression of Ferroptosis
abstract: Impaired healing in diabetic wounds presents a major clinical challenge, driven by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated cellular responses. Herein, a poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)-polyethylenimine (PLGA-PEI)-based nanoplatform for the sustained delivery of vitamin K1 (VK1) was developed to enhance diabetic wound healing through ferroptosis suppression involving ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1). The formulated PLGA-PEI-VK1 nanoparticles exhibited a relatively uniform size distribution, sustained VK1 release, good hemocompatibility, and enhanced antioxidant activity. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that VK1-associated targets were closely related to redox regulation, cell migration, and ferroptosis-associated processes. In vitro, PLGA-PEI-VK1 nanoparticles protected L929 fibroblasts from advanced glycation end products-induced injury; enhanced cell proliferation and migration; attenuated reactive oxygen species accumulation, intracellular Fe 2+ overload, and lipid peroxidation; restored antioxidant capacity; and increased FSP1 expression. In a diabetic mouse model, PLGA-PEI-VK1 nanoparticles significantly accelerated wound closure and improved tissue regeneration and matrix remodeling, supporting its therapeutic potential in vivo. Mechanistically, molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay, and molecular dynamics simulations supported an interaction between VK1 and FSP1. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of FSP1 markedly impaired the anti-ferroptotic effects of PLGA-PEI-VK1, supporting an important role for FSP1 in VK1-dependent ferroptosis suppression. These findings demonstrate that PLGA-PEI-mediated delivery of VK1 promotes diabetic wound repair, at least in part, through FSP1-associated suppression of ferroptosis and provide a potential nanotherapeutic strategy for diabetic wound management.

title: The Sv DC Field: Large-scale and Hierarchical Functions Regulator
Enhanced Endosomal Trafficking Mediated by the Proton-Activated Chloride Channel Underlies Peripheral Sensitization in Neuropathic Pain
Feedforward Inhibition Mediated by Preoptic Area Parvalbumin Neurons Contributes to Orexin Induced Active Arousal from Anesthesia
Gelatin-Mediated Interfacial Engineering of Cellulose-Based Phase Change Foams for Temperature-Adaptive Thermal Regulation
abstract: Thermally insulating materials are used for thermal management in various applications, but conventional materials only block heat transfer, leading to a substantial trade-off between preventing external heat penetration and retaining indoor heat. Here, we report a temperature-adaptive bio-composite foam (CPF) constructed via gelatin-mediated interfacial engineering. The material features an isotropic hierarchical porous structure with a maximum porosity of 95.9%, exhibiting a thermal conductivity of 0.039 W/(m·K) and a noise reduction coefficient (NRC) of 0.54. Benefiting from the anchoring effect of gelatin on phase-change microcapsules (PCMCs) at the plateau borders, the foam withstands a load up to 481 times its own weight without deformation. It also possesses an enthalpy of 140.7 J/g, effectively reconciling the trade-off between thermal insulation and heat dissipation in enclosed spaces. Moreover, the reversible molecular-scale structural design endows the CPF with closed-loop recyclability. This study provides a promising strategy for the development of all-weather, temperature-adaptive thermal management materials.

title: Cell Reprogramming: Therapeutic Advances and Challenges
abstract: Cell reprogramming, which forcibly alters cell fate, offers a novel therapeutic strategy for various refractory diseases.Unlike previous reviews focused on a single disease context or a single reprogramming modality, this review is organized around therapeutic applications.It summarizes advances in direct reprogramming, partial reprogramming, and cell fusion-induced reprogramming, and further compares their mechanisms, challenges in clinical translation, and safety boundaries.In oncology, reprogramming cancer cells into antigen-presenting cells elicits durable antitumor immunity and remodels the tumor microenvironment, whereas converting cancer cells into nonmalignant somatic cells can reduce their malignant phenotype and tumorigenic potential.In neurodegenerative diseases, direct reprogramming has converted fibroblasts or astrocytes into functional dopaminergic and cortical neurons both in vitro and in vivo.In mouse models of progeria and natural aging, partial reprogramming strategies significantly extend lifespan, ameliorate multi-organ pathology, and enhance tissue regenerative capacity.However, the strength and reproducibility of these findings vary across experimental models, and reported therapeutic benefits do not necessarily establish complete, stable, or safe cell-fate conversion.Against this predominantly preclinical background, ER-100 is the first regenerative therapy based on partial epigenetic reprogramming to receive FDA Investigational New Drug approval and enter clinical testing.It therefore provides an important reference point for the transition from animal studies to human trials.Cell fusion-induced reprogramming has context-dependent roles in tumor immunity.Fusion between tumor cells and immune cells may promote malignant progression.In contrast, dendritic celltumor cell fusion vaccines and chimeric exosomes can activate antitumor immune responses in Downloaded from https://spj.science.orgon October 24, 2026 preclinical models and early clinical studies.Major barriers to clinical translation include low reprogramming efficiency, an incompletely defined safety window, and the need to select in vivo or ex vivo strategies according to disease context.In addition, insufficient delivery efficiency, poor targeting, and long-term tumorigenic risk remain important constraints on clinical application.Looking ahead, single-cell multi-omics and artificial intelligence may help optimize reprogramming factor combinations, while non-viral systems may improve targeted delivery.Integration with tissue engineering may further facilitate clinical translation across oncology, aging, regenerative medicine, autoimmune diseases, and neuropsychiatric disorders.

The temperature sensitivity of soil CO2 release is modified by virus-bacteria interactions
abstract: The temperature sensitivity (Q 10 ) of soil carbon (C) release is key to predicting carbon-climate feedback, yet omitting microbial interactions, especially with soil viruses, introduces substantial uncertainty.To address this, we performed 30-day and 365-day incubations with metagenomics and metatranscriptomics profiling.We found that soil viruses significantly decreased Q 10 during 30-day incubation.Over 365-day incubation, however, their effects on microbial metabolism and Q 10 were temperaturedependent.The relative abundance of pathways related to viral replication, including those for lytic cycle initiation (e.g., propanoate metabolism decreased by 15.24%), and the energy supply (e.g., lipoic acid metabolism decreased by 20.95%), became less abundant as temperature rose from 15°C to 35°C.Metatranscriptomics data confirmed this trend, with upregulation of metabolic functions related to viral infection and replication at 15°C.Thus, temperature-driven variations in viral activity underlie the contrasting roles of soil viruses in regulating Q 10 .This study provides the first evidence of temperature-dependent viral regulation of microbial metabolism and Q 10 , highlighting the need to incorporate soil viruses into carbon-climate models.
